title: Second recursive descent branch
statement: Let $E,s,w,i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean-valued oracle on four indices and Boolean words, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a register state. Suppose $s\leq w$, $i+1\leq w$, the recursive-call property holds at level $i$, and $\mathrm{st}$ satisfies the level-$(i+1)$ invariant with parameters $s,w$; also suppose its midpoint register is less than $2^w$ and $M_1\leq 2^w$. Starting at phase $0$ of the push loop for the true phase bit, with the target register set to the original midpoint, the midpoint register set to $M_1$, and the popped-endpoint register set to the original target, the machine reaches the phase-1 success site when level-$i$ reachability holds from the original midpoint to the original target, and the phase-1 failure site otherwise. For some $M_2\leq 2^w$, its final source register is the original midpoint, its midpoint register is $M_2$, and its popped-endpoint register is the original source; every configuration before the final one satisfies the guard requiring valid instructions and all registers at most $2^{w\cdot w}$.

the recursive-call property holds at level $i$
$\mathrm{st}$ satisfies the level-$(i+1)$ invariant with parameters $s,w$
